methods.description: In lowest terms, factorise the denominator. Only primes 2 and/or 5 give a terminating decimal; any other prime gives a recurring decimal.
Cancel common factors first; a prime in an unsimplified denominator may disappear. Then apply the same denominator test.

sourceReview.locator: Whole governing terminating/recurring clause and complete single-digit denominator example
sourceReview.observation: Read the complete governing clause and both example boxes. Classification is Stage 4; current parent teaches recurring notation. No later-stage mathematics is used.
sourceReview.adjustments: Preserve current Stage 4 classification scope, original practice and all three Theory steps.

sourceReview.locator: Complete terminating/recurring definitions, notation and calculator conversion scaffolds
sourceReview.observation: Read the complete decimal definitions, notation and unfilled scaffold. Terminating means ends, recurring repeats forever. This source supports meanings; it does not itself teach the denominator criterion.
sourceReview.adjustments: No new notation conversion method is added; prerequisite already teaches dot/bar notation.

sourceReview.locator: Whole filled investigation 18: denominator prime factors, explicit criterion and lowest-term counterexample
sourceReview.observation: Read the entire filled investigation 18, both four-fraction tables, explicit prime-factor conclusion, Lily counterexample and 16/30 task. Personally viewed original image45 at original detail: a decorative cartoon child, no mathematical labels. The quoted false claim about 15/30 is deliberately a student error to explain, not an accepted answer.
sourceReview.adjustments: E0 adapts filled investigation18a numbers 79/80 and11/14 to37/80 and23/28, preserving factor-test method with manageable nontrivial numbers. E1 adapts filled Lily15/30 and16/30 simplification contrast to33/60 and34/51; unlike original30, denominator51 leaves3 after cancellation. Both are source-authored adaptations, not copies of published practice. Explicit lowest-terms qualification retained.

substantiveCorrections: All four quiz stems explicitly request both correct classification and valid reason, resolving distractors with right classifications but invalid reasons.
q1 option1 explanation no longer falsely says numerator plays no part at all: numerator can cancel factors before testing.
q2 option3 explanation gives terminating counterexample7/20 rather than declaring divisibility irrelevant.
q4 solution identifies prime3 correctly rather than grammatically calling composite9 a prime.
